Noah G.: Hey folks, I'm slated for my first on-call rotation next week. Quick checklist: who signs me off for solo shifts, where do I find runbooks for cache and failover, and is there a safe way to rehearse a P1/P0 flow?

Maya R. (oncall-lead): Welcome Noah! :wave: Sign-off after two shadowed shifts + one tabletop sim + buddy thumbs-up. Runbooks live at https://wiki.internal/redwood/runbooks/oncall (SSO/VPN required).

Ops Bot: PagerDuty invite sent; user Noah G. added to rotation (pending acceptance). Sandbox namespace created for sim: ns=oncall-sandbox-174812.

Ivy Z.: I can buddy your first shift. For rehearsal, use the sandbox and DevEx CLI: `rw-sim alert create --namespace oncall-sandbox-174812 --severity P1 --scenario partial-degradation` — this will create a fake PD alert and mock channel.

DevEx: Also run `rw incident checklist start --dry-run` on the devbox; it walks you through the triage steps and expected commands without touching prod. Docs: https://redwood.internal/devex/oncall-sim

Noah G.: Great, thanks. Any immediate triage commands I should memorize?

Ivy Z.: Short list: `kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide`, `kubectl logs -n inference <pod> -c runtime --since=10m`, `curl -fS http://health.internal/ready`, and check APM traces. If you see data loss signs, escalate immediately.

Maya R. (oncall-lead): One policy note: ack within 2 minutes, if you cannot access tooling within 10 minutes escalate to the secondary. For post-incident writeups use the template at https://redwood.internal/postmortems/template.md — include timeline, impact, RCA, and owners.

Noah G.: Perfect. I'll accept the PD invite, try the dry-run tonight, and pair with Ivy on Monday. Thanks all! :pray:
